analysis.title: Global House View: Macro Perspective, November 2026
key_insights: Aegon AM is underweight global equities and overweight fixed income, with the overweight concentrated in investment-grade credit. Stated reason: recent AI-related share weakness shows scrutiny of valuations, funding costs and returns on large capital expenditures.
Equity underweight rests on near-term risk-reward. Earnings growth and AI investment are supportive, but energy-price volatility and inflation risk pressure margins and discount rates.
Fixed-income overweight is not a duration call. Persistent inflation and fiscal pressure leave government bonds exposed to higher yields, so government bonds stay neutral.

Investment-grade credit is preferred over lower-quality credit because higher all-in yields give income and issuer balance sheets are stronger. Rising debt-financed AI spending and spread risk call for issuer and sector selection.
Commodities are neutral. Energy exposure can cushion renewed inflation shocks, but any resolution of the Iran conflict would sharply lower energy prices.
Cash is underweight to deploy into investment-grade bonds for longer-horizon income. The view reflects relative returns, not an expectation of imminent central-bank rate cuts.

All equity regions (US, Europe, UK, Japan, Asia ex-Japan) and REITs are neutral within the overall equity underweight. Valuation and earnings support is offset by tech concentration, energy sensitivity, trade uncertainty and financing costs.
Securitized assets are underweight in the US, with a preference for longer duration in investment grade. Aegon AM stays constructive on European ABS and CLOs because of the spread pick-up.
High yield and EM debt are neutral. Aegon AM prefers investment grade for additional credit exposure. Weaker issuers face refinancing costs and earnings risk.
USD, EUR, JPY and GBP are all neutral. Rate differentials, energy prices and risk appetite create two-sided risks.
The Fed held its target range at 3.75%-4.00% on October 28. Aegon AM says it is premature to assume a renewed easing cycle or that the inflation shock is fully priced into bonds.
Views are as of October 26, 2026 on a 3-month horizon.

sector_views.rationale: AI-related valuation scrutiny, funding costs, energy volatility and inflation outweigh supportive earnings growth.
Higher all-in yields and stronger issuer balance sheets than lower-quality credit.
Higher yields and defensive value are balanced by energy-driven inflation, heavy sovereign borrowing and tightening risk.
Carry supports returns, but refinancing costs and earnings disappointments leave weaker issuers exposed.
Energy cushions inflation shocks, but a resolution of the Iran conflict would sharply cut prices.
Rental income and possible relief from lower yields are offset by inflation, refinancing costs and uneven property fundamentals.

earnings_insights: The report cites strong corporate earnings and AI investment as supports for equities but gives no specific EPS or revenue figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed held rates. Aegon AM says it is premature to assume a renewed easing cycle given persistent inflation.

risk_factors: AI-related valuation, funding-cost and capex-return scrutiny
Fiscal pressure and heavy sovereign borrowing pushing yields higher
Refinancing costs and earnings disappointments for lower-quality credit
Energy-import dependence in Europe and Japan
Sharp fall in energy prices if the Iran conflict resolves (for the commodities and UK energy and mining exposure)
vol_and_positioning: Recent credit-market volatility reinforces the need for issuer selection.
Japanese government bond volatility is cited as a risk to Japanese equity valuations.
The report cites concentrated market leadership as leaving equities vulnerable to disappointments.
geopolitical: Conflicting diplomatic and supply-disruption developments around the Iran conflict are causing sharp oil-price swings. Aegon AM says any resolution would sharply lower energy prices.

key_data_points.context: Fed held rates at its October 28, 2026 meeting.
key_data_points.anchor: The Federal Reserve held its target range at a range of between 3.75% and 4.00% at its meeting on October 28.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong corporate earnings and substantial AI investment remain supportive of equities.
tension_points.bear_case: Recent weakness in AI-related shares shows scrutiny of valuations, funding costs and capex returns. Energy volatility and inflation pressure margins and discount rates.

tension_points.bull_case: Energy exposure can cushion renewed inflation shocks.
tension_points.bear_case: Any resolution of the Iran conflict would sharply lower energy prices and reverse the geopolitical premium.

theme_stances.key_argument: Weakness in AI-related shares shifts attention from the scale of investment to the timing of returns, funding needs and rate sensitivity.
theme_stances.evidence: Recent weakness in AI-related shares highlights growing scrutiny of valuations

theme_stances.key_argument: Higher all-in yields and stronger issuer balance sheets make investment grade a more defensive source of income than equities or lower-quality credit.
